goodbye-mars: Just return the exact sentence from the subject; watch the space before the exclamation mark.
system-logger: Put the fixed log prefix in front of the message, including its colon and trailing space.
universal-greeting: Match the language code to its greeting; any code you do not know gets an empty string.
average-calc: Walk from start toward end by step, add up and count the values, then divide; handle a zero or wrong-direction step.
multiplication-table: Loop from 1 to 10 and print one line per product in the exact 'n x i = result' format.
unit-converter: Check there are exactly three arguments and the number parses, then pick the formula for the unit pair; round to two decimals.
strlen: The String class already knows its own length.
count-char: Go through the string one character at a time and count the ones equal to the target.
digitlen: Keep dividing by ten until nothing is left, counting steps; zero and negative numbers still have digits.
rotate-array: Reduce the count modulo the length so negative or big counts wrap, then put each element at its shifted index.
reverse-array: Build a new array of the same size, filling it from the end of the original.
sort-array: Any simple sort works: repeatedly swap neighbours that are out of order until none are.
almost-palindrom: Ignore case; a word that is already a palindrome does not count, otherwise try removing each character once.
factorial: Multiply every number from 1 up to n together; remember 0! is 1.
next-prime: Start just above n (never below 2) and step up until you reach a number with no divisor up to its square root.
todo-list: Keep a count of how many tasks are stored; ignore adds past capacity and indexes outside that count. Pad descriptions to a fixed width when printing.
time-tracker: Parse both times with a strict pattern, work out the difference in minutes, then step up to hours, days, months as each count reaches 120.
date-formatter: Use a UTC Calendar to get day, month and year, compare the format ignoring case, and only reformat when the format is one of the three allowed.
area-calculator: Each overload just applies its own formula; the extra boolean only exists so Java can tell the signatures apart.
factorial-master: One version loops and multiplies a running product; the other calls itself with n-1 and stops at 0 or 1.
flexisort: Bubble sort swaps neighbours and can stop early after a pass with no swaps; insertion sort shifts larger values right to make room for each new one.
double-linked-list: Track head, tail and size; start a search from whichever end is closer, and relink the neighbours' next and prev when removing.
circular-linked-list: The last node points back to head, so walking never hits null; when removing the head, fix the last node's next too.
single-linked-list: To remove index i, stop at the node just before it and point that node past the target; removing the head needs no walking.
harmonious-fusion: Keep one pointer per array, copy the smaller front value each time, then copy whatever is left.
distinct-substring-length: Slide a window: remember where each character was last seen and move the window start past a repeat.
is-anagram: Lowercase both strings and check they contain exactly the same characters the same number of times, spaces included.
spiral-matrix: Keep four edges (top, bottom, left, right), fill one side at a time, and pull that edge inward after each.
maximal-square: For each 1, the largest square ending there is one more than the smallest of the squares above, to the left and diagonally up-left.
steady-sequence: Put the numbers in a set and only start counting upward from numbers whose predecessor is not in the set.
day-of-week: Parse the date with java.time, turn the day name into a DayOfWeek enum, and look for a temporal adjuster that jumps to the next one; catch failures.
monthly-period: Period.between gives years and months; put the dates in order first, then build the text with singular/plural words and 'and' only when both parts exist.
age-finder: Parse with yyyy-MM-dd and measure the years between that date and today; any parse failure or a date in the future means -1.
html-validator: Find every opening and closing tag in order and keep a stack: push on open, pop and compare on close; at the end the stack must be empty.
breakdown-url: Write one regex with groups for protocol, domain, optional port, optional path and optional query; add only the parts that matched, path defaults to '/'.
config-protector: Per sensitive key, match whole lines that start with exactly that key and '=', and swap the value for as many stars as it has characters.
singleton-blueprint: The class must control its own creation: hide the constructor, keep one shared private instance, and hand it out lazily from a static method.
builder-blueprint: RegexBuilder should be an interface; the concrete builder collects pieces in its list and getResult turns that list into a Regex.
factory-blueprint: Both products must share the Product type; the factory picks which one to create from the type string and returns null for anything else.
top-frequents: Count with a map and remember where each number first appears; order by count descending, then by first position, and take up to k.
longest-common-prefix: Start with the first word as the prefix and keep shortening it until every other word starts with it; watch out for empty input.
first-unique: Make two passes: count every character first, then return the first one whose count is exactly one, or an underscore.
valid-sudoku: Ignore dots and make sure no digit repeats in any row, column or 3x3 box; sets keyed by row, column and box make this easy.
armstrong-number: Count the digits, raise each digit to that power, add them up and compare with the original number.
perfect-number: Add up every divisor smaller than the number itself (pairs up to the square root are enough); numbers below 2 are never perfect.
